:::{#cor-entropy-quantization-diverges}
#### Entropy of a quantized random variable grows without bound

In the setting of @thm-entropy-quantization,

$$\entropyf{X^\Delta} \to \infty \quad \text{as } \Delta \to 0.$$

:::

::: proof

By @thm-entropy-quantization,
$\entropyf{X^\Delta} + \log \Delta \to \entropyf{X}$ as $\Delta \to 0$.
Moving $\log \Delta$ to the other side,

$$\entropyf{X^\Delta} = \paren{\entropyf{X^\Delta} + \log \Delta} - \log \Delta.$$

The first quantity on the right tends to $\entropyf{X}$,
a finite number:
the density is continuous and $0$ outside a bounded interval,
so $-\p(X=x) \log \p(X=x)$ is continuous there, with the convention $0 \log 0 = 0$,
and a continuous function has a finite integral over a bounded interval.
Also, $-\log \Delta \to \infty$ as $\Delta \to 0$,
so $\entropyf{X^\Delta} \to \infty$.

:::
